entities.summary:
2009–2010 pandemic of swine influenza caused by h1n1 influenza virus. The 2009 swine flu pandemic occurred between 2009-03-01 and 2010-08-10, affecting the global population. The outbreak took place during a time of increased global interconnectedness, facilitated by air travel. This global spread of the virus resulted in a significant loss of life and a substantial economic impact. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on June 11, 2009.

The impact of the pandemic was felt worldwide, with the United States, Mexico, and China among the most affected countries. The rapid spread of the virus was facilitated by the increased mobility of people during the spring and summer of 2009. The pandemic resulted in the deaths of an estimated 150,000 to 575,000 people globally.

The 2009 swine flu pandemic had significant long-term consequences, including the acceleration of the development of vaccines and antiviral medications. The pandemic also led to increased global cooperation and preparedness for future pandemics. The virus itself was declared to be no longer a global health threat by the WHO on August 10, 2010.

The 2009 swine flu pandemic will be remembered as a turning point in the history of modern medicine, highlighting the importance of global cooperation and the rapid development of medical countermeasures in the face of a rapidly spreading pandemic.
